title: Generated Context versus Governed State: Functional Conditions for Accountable Longitudinal Clinical Reasoning
abstract: arXiv:2608.14804v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have become the dominant interface of clinical artificial intelligence, yet the interface they expose (text in, text out, one context window at a time) maintains no explicit, persistent, governed representation of what is currently true about a patient. This paper argues that longitudinal clinical reasoning is a state-estimation problem under partial observability, and that the axis on which clinical AI succeeds or fails is not the fluency of the model reading the record but the governance of the patient state it reasons over. translated_title: 生成上下文与受治理状态：可问责纵向临床推理的功能条件
translated_abstract: 大型语言模型（LLMs）已成为临床人工智能的主导界面，然而它们所暴露的界面（文本输入、文本输出、一次一个上下文窗口）并未维护关于患者当前真实状态的显式、持久且受治理的表示。本文认为，纵向临床推理是在部分可观测性下的状态估计问题，临床人工智能成功或失败的关键轴不在于模型阅读记录的流畅性，而在于其推理所依据的患者状态的治理程度。我们区分了生成上下文与受治理状态；分离了临床人工智能习惯性混淆的五个对象（真实状态、观测、证据、信念和模拟状态）；定义了一个分层治理标准，任何临床人工智能系统均可据此进行审计；并表明可问责性的操作性定义可分解为四个信息需求：不可变电子健康记录、可追溯的推理过程、可验证的状态更新以及可解释的决策输出。
tldr: 本文提出纵向临床推理应被视为部分可观测下的状态估计问题，并主张通过区分生成上下文与受治理状态、定义分层治理标准及四个信息需求，为临床AI系统建立可审计的可问责性框架。
en_tdlr: This paper argues that longitudinal clinical reasoning should be framed as state estimation under partial observability, and proposes distinguishing generated context from governed state, defining a tiered governance standard, and decomposing accountability into four information requirements to establish an auditable accountability framework for clinical AI systems.
